meta: AI is good, but some jobs the seller must do themselves. Bit stops Mark before four: prices and stock, product claims, customer data, and caring for regulars.

muc.title: Handing everything to AI
muc.text: AI seems so good that Mark plans to hand every job in the shop to it. Bit quickly stops him.

muc.title: Prices, discounts, stock
muc.text: The first job not to hand over: deciding prices, discounts or stock levels. If AI gets one number wrong, the shop loses real money.

muc.title: Promises about what a product does
muc.text: The second: claims about what a product does, especially cosmetics, food or health products. Overstating them breaks advertising rules.

muc.title: Customer data
muc.text: The third: putting customers' phone numbers and addresses into a personal AI account. That's other people's data, as in the data part of video 121.

muc.title: Caring for loyal customers
muc.text: The last: looking after regular customers and handling difficult complaints. Customers remember a sincere thank-you longer than any polished words.

muc.title: Split the work with AI
muc.text: Draw a two-column table, jobs AI drafts and jobs you decide yourself, and pin it where you work so the whole shop follows it.
